reader.title: Killing of Martin Wilson
bases: A posse shot and killed Martin Wilson, and the item gives the killing as punishment 'for having attempted to outrage' a white woman, not as resistance to arrest (A1).

A1 says a posse killed Wilson for an alleged attempted assault on a white woman, which fits a killing under the pretext of justice; the item does not give the posse's size, whether it had legal authority, or whether Wilson resisted, so the verdict rests on one brief.
Only one undated brief in an Arkansas weekly's news column reports the killing (A1); no second report was found.

summary.text: The killing of Martin Wilson was the shooting of a Black man by a posse at a place printed as Malton, Alabama, reported at the end of August 1888.
He was accused of having attempted to assault a white woman, and the only known report gave that accusation as the reason he was killed.
According to a brief news item, Wilson, described as "a negro," was "shot and killed by a posse" at Malton for having attempted to "outrage a highly respectable white lady."
The item did not name the woman or any member of the posse, nor did it give the date of the killing, the county, or how the posse found him.
It also did not say whether Wilson was being arrested or resisted, or whether the posse acted under any legal authority.
No report of an inquest, arrest or other follow-up appears in the coverage.
The Forrest City Times of Arkansas carried the story on September 1, 1888, as a single sentence in its "Domestic" column of national briefs.
There it sat between a congressional nomination in Iowa and a girl struck by lightning on Pike's Peak, with no headline or comment of its own.
The sentence stated the accusation as the cause of the killing and described the woman as "highly respectable," without naming a source for the charge.
The coverage includes no other report of the killing in either the white or the Black press.
